IOER.revision_evidence: IOER is a discontinued administered rate. Its final observation is 2021-07-28, the day before the Board of Governors consolidated interest on excess reserves and interest on required reserves into a single rate on reserve balances; IORB begins 2021-07-29, so the two abut with no overlap and no gap. Like IORB it was set by the Board and announced in advance of its effective date rather than measured from a reporting population, so there is no filer whose restatement could revise it, and the series has been closed for over five years. This claim is weaker than the IORB declaration beside it and the difference is deliberate: no ALFRED vintage comparison was run for IOER. Neither the device nor the cloud session that added this field had a network route to ALFRED on 8 September 2026, so the never-revised claim rests on the administrative argument and on the series being closed, not on observed vintages. IORB's rests on 1864 identical values across three vintages.
IOER.note: Added 8 September 2026 so the administered leg of SOFR - IORB can be priced before 2021-07-29. Without it the funding panel begins in July 2021 and contains neither September 2019 nor March 2020. The splice is declared in contract.FEATURE_FIELDS and guarded by build_daily_panel rule 7, which raises if IOER and IORB ever report the same reference date. OUTSTANDING: verify against two IOER vintages spanning 2021-07-28 and replace revision_evidence when a route to ALFRED is available.

IORB.revision_evidence: Three ALFRED vintages of IORB -- 2024-09-01, 2026-09-03 and 2026-09-04 -- agree on every overlapping observation: 1130 identical values from 2021-07-29 to 2024-08-31 across a two-year vintage gap, and 1864 identical values from 2021-07-29 to 2026-09-04. No observation has been restated. The rate is administered by the Board of Governors and announced in advance of its effective date, which the vintages themselves show: the 2026-09-03 vintage already carries observations dated 2026-09-04, and the 2026-09-04 vintage carries through 2026-09-08. Latest vintage is therefore point-in-time for this field and for no other field of this source.
IORB.note: Deliberately conservative. IORB for a date is knowable before that date; a one-day record-date lag against the H.15 publication time purges more than the evidence requires, which splits.py establishes as the safe direction. The number is the human's decision of 8 September 2026, not a derivation.

cross_section.note: Each bulk extract covers a filing window and carries one dominant monthly cross-section plus amendment and straggler filings for adjacent months, and the stragglers are not a universe: in the 2026-07 extract, July has 325 reporting series and the other five report dates have between 1 and 5. A ref_date below this floor is excluded from the panel and recorded in the quality report, with the SUBMISSIONTYPE mix of its submissions alongside as a corroborating record that is never a filter. The floor counts distinct SERIESID and never a value total, because the values are what the floor exists to make trustworthy. It is an absolute count rather than a fraction of a trailing median because the trailing median is itself computed from straggler months: on this extract the straggler counts have a median of 4, so a quarter-of-median rule would set the floor at 1 and admit the 1-series April cross-section it was written to reject. 200 is about 60 percent of the 325 observed in the one complete month available when it was calibrated. The 26-archive backfill of 7 September 2026 shows that one absolute count does not hold across the published history: the reporting universe falls from 728 series in 2010 to about 310 in 2026, so 200 is 27 percent of the early universe and 64 percent of the current one. A per-era declared absolute is the decided remedy and is not implemented here; the observed counts each era entry would be calibrated from are in the Track A decision memo of 7 September 2026.

identities.name: series_assets_reconcile_to_liabilities_and_net_assets
identities.tolerance_note: An absolute bound, deliberately, and provisional. The case for a relative bound is real -- the identity is scale-free and one absolute number is about 35 parts per million of the largest cross-section observed and a quarter of the smallest -- but the cross-section coverage floor rejects exactly the small months that made the case, so post-floor one cross-section is admitted and the residual on it is 0.312 USD billions on 9005 USD billions of net assets. Recalibrating a shared-schema shape against a single observation is the failure the change was meant to prevent, so the change is deferred until at least three cross-sections are admitted; see docs/DATA_QUALITY_DECISIONS.md. This bound is therefore calibrated against one admitted cross-section and has not been tested against a second. It is an ingestion check, not evidence that a cross-section represents the market. The schema now accepts relative_ppm alongside absolute, so lifting the deferral is a one-line change to this declaration and not a change to the contract.

sec_nmfp.limitation: As-filed data may contain reporting errors and becomes available after month-end. Refusal is per table. A table the archive does not carry costs exactly the panel fields it supplies, which then have no observation from that archive -- absent, never zero -- and the archive is read for everything else; metadata/sec_nmfp_archives.json records this per archive as a refusals entry of kind absent_fields naming those fields. A table that is present with a column the adapter reads under a changed name refuses the whole archive (kind unreadable), because a renamed column reaches the parser as an absent value and yields a silently partial series that still satisfies the balance-sheet identity; such an archive contributes no observations and is not placed under data/raw/. NMFP_SUBMISSION.tsv is the one table whose absence is unreadable rather than a cost in fields, because without it no row can be attributed to a series or a report date. Schema compatibility across the published history was diffed archive by archive on 7 September 2026: of 97 declared archives, all 97 are read; the 71 filed before 2024-06-10 carry no NMFP_DLYSHAREHOLDERFLOWREPORT.tsv, because daily shareholder-flow reporting began with Form N-MFP3, so mmf_gross_subscriptions, mmf_gross_redemptions and mmf_net_flow have no observation for those filing windows. Header compatibility is not value compatibility: every column this adapter reads is present under the same name back to 2010q4, but INVESTMENTCATEGORY is a categorical the adapter matches on by value and its vocabulary was rewritten at the 2016-04 report month (Treasury Debt to U.S. Treasury Debt, and every other label with it) and again at 2024-06 (U.S. Government Agency Debt split into coupon-paying and no-coupon variants; the Other Repurchase Agreement label reworded). The accepted and deliberately excluded category strings are therefore declared per era in NMFP_INVESTMENT_CATEGORY_ERAS, enumerated from all 97 archives rather than from documentation. A category string an era does not declare raises rather than matching nothing, and a report month in no declared era loses mmf_treasury_holdings, mmf_repo_holdings and mmf_on_rrp for that cross-section and nothing else. The last era is bounded by the newest report month the declared archive set carries, because the vocabulary is still moving.

release_lag.note: The bulk extract is a monthly compilation of as-filed submissions; rows inherit the immutable extract retrieval timestamp rather than the filing deadline or report date.

treasury_auctions.limitation: treasury_settlement is one aggregate: the announced offering amounts of every auction sharing an issue_date, summed and converted to USD billions. All security types are aggregated and SOMA add-ons are included, so tenor structure and the private-versus-Fed split are not represented. Both omissions matter to a repo model specifically. Bill and coupon settlements have different collateral and reserve-drain profiles, and bill supply is close to the centre of the 2018-19 episode this project exists to model. Fed SOMA add-ons do not drain private cash, so a total that includes them overstates the private-sector drain, and overstates it most when the Fed is rolling over most heavily -- which is to say in the regimes of interest. security_type, security_term and soma_accepted are all present in the snapshot and are not read; splitting the series needs no new download. This note replaces one that said announcement and result vintages must be separated to avoid using auction outcomes too early. That risk is avoided by construction and was never the live one: record_date drives available_at and is part of vintage_id, so an announced but unsettled auction is visible from its publication date and not before, and the adapter reads offering_amt alone and never total_accepted, high_yield or bid_to_cover. It cannot use auction outcomes too early because it does not read auction outcomes. A limitation describing a risk the adapter avoids absolutely, while silent on the one it creates, reads as vigilance.
treasury_auctions.provider: U.S. Department of the Treasury Fiscal Data

release_lag.note: Fiscal Data defines record_date as the publication date; end-of-day availability conservatively avoids assuming an intraday publication time.

treasury_auctions.reviewed_note: Structural-zero semantics have not yet been reviewed against the Treasury auction data dictionary; the empty declaration is not a finding.
